name: Ajanta Pharma Ltd
tagline: A large-cap branded-generics compounder with primary filings that confirm the quality — FY26 crossed Rs 5,000 Cr revenue / Rs 1,000 Cr PAT and Q1 FY27 accelerated — tracked by a trusted user and held as an 18%+ concentrated bet by another
business_overview: Ajanta Pharma is a branded-generics-focused pharmaceutical company (~70%+ of revenue) with a strong India presence (ophthalmology, cardiology, dermatology rankings among market leaders), a growing US generics/ANDA business, and expanding Asia/Africa branded generics plus an Africa institutional business, running a basket of 500+ products with roughly half first-to-market.
fundamentals_table: ~50% (Rs 32 first interim declared with Q1 FY27)

fundamentals_narrative: The primary-document read confirms the sustained quality the sentiment pass described. FY26 (year ended Mar-2026): revenue Rs 5,452.9 Cr (+17% YoY), PAT Rs 1,056 Cr (+~15% YoY), EBITDA Rs 1,395 Cr (26% margin; adjusted EBITDA Rs 1,498 Cr, +18%), ROCE 33%, return on net worth 25%, near-zero debt — US generics +49% and India +14% led. Q1 FY27 (June-2026) then accelerated: revenue Rs 1,626 Cr (+25% YoY), PAT Rs 334 Cr (+31% YoY), gross margin ~80%, adjusted EBITDA margin ~28%, with US generics +57% to Rs 487 Cr and India branded generics +24% to Rs 509 Cr; Asia dipped on Middle-East supply-chain disruption. Working capital tightened (receivable days to ~94, inventory days to ~72). Management's FY27 guidance is high-teens overall revenue growth — India and Asia mid-to-high-teens, Africa branded + institutional high double-digit, but US explicitly guided to only mid-single-digit for FY27 with price erosion expected, so the Q1 US surge is a launch-timing spike, not the run-rate. Dividend policy remains generous (~50% payout; Rs 32 first interim with Q1 FY27); no buyback since May-2024. Execution consistency is corroborated by harsh.beria93's multi-year primary-source notes.
technical_read: Not independently pulled beyond price context — the stock is at a fresh 52-week high of Rs 3,796.95 after roughly a 90%+ one-year move, so a good deal of the re-rating has already happened.
